Cokhāmeḷā
------------------------------------------
Untouchability (aspṛśyatā) has been an ugly blot on the Hindu society. As if to deliver a blow to such narrow concepts and practices, many great saints have been born among these untouchables. They had to be accepted and honoured by the elitist groups and castes by the sheer power of their spiritual glory.
One such great saint was चोखामेऌआ. He lived in the thirteenth century in the holy city of Paṇḍharāpura (in Maha-rashtra). It was his wont to have a dip in the Bhīmā river early in the morning, circumambulate the temple of पाण्डुरङ्ग (also called Viṭṭhala, an aspect of विष्णु or कृष्ण) from outside, bow down to the deity from the main gate and sing songs in his praise, mostly composed by himself. The proud and prejudiced priests tried their best to humiliate him and even harm him; but were humbled in the end since the Lord was on his side. They were obliged to accept his greatness and honour him.
As in the lives of many other saints, miracles are said to have happened in his life also. He died when the wall he was building, along with other workmen, collapsed. His समाधि (grave) is still to be seen at Paṇḍharāpura, opposite to that of नाम्देव्, another great saint who was his contemporary. He has left some nice अभङ्गस् (devotional songs in Marāṭhi language) in which he describes his travails due to social prejudices and the acts of grace by God.
See ABHAṄGAS and NĀMDEV.
